story_type: C-130 air tanker lays a retardant line on a mountain wildfire
hook: 3,000 gallons out the back of a C-130 in under 5 seconds.
narration: This C-130 can empty three thousand gallons of fire retardant in under five seconds.
In June 2012, the Waldo Canyon fire was burning in the mountains near Colorado Springs.
Wyoming Air National Guard and Air Force Reserve crews took off in C-130s fitted with special tanks.
The system is called MAFFS. Compressed air blasts the retardant out through a nozzle at the back of the plane.
The crews flew low over the ridges, looking for the edge of the fire.
Seen from above, the big tanker looked tiny against the forest.
[short pause] Then the crew hit the release.
The retardant came out in a red wall and laid a line across the trees.
outcome: Within days, MAFFS crews had made twenty-three drops on the Waldo Canyon fire, about sixty thousand gallons of retardant.
title: C-130 drops retardant on a wildfire
description:
In June 2012, C-130s from the Wyoming Air National Guard's 153rd Airlift Wing and the Air Force Reserve's 302nd Airlift Wing flew Modular Airborne Fire Fighting System missions over the wildfires near Colorado Springs, Colorado, including the Waldo Canyon fire.

Footage: U.S. Air Force video by Senior Airman Robert Harnden, 2d Combat Camera Squadron, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/148130
